summary: Flutter audio settings now match the web response to hotplug: an unavailable selected route is retained while the system temporarily reports no devices; when a non-empty list returns without that route, selection moves to the first available device and an accessible warning asks the user to verify audio. Explicitly choosing a device clears the warning.

checks.name: State behavior for empty then recovered device enumeration
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test --no-pub test/app_state_test.dart --plain-name 'warns and selects an available device when the chosen mic is disconnected'
checks.observation: The chosen route survives a temporarily empty enumeration. When a replacement list arrives, the first available microphone is selected, the connected speaker remains selected, and the web-equivalent warning is set.

checks.name: Accessible audio settings warning UI
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test --no-pub test/workspace_screen_test.dart --plain-name 'announces when the selected audio device disconnects'
checks.observation: The warning renders in audio settings and is exposed as a live region.

checks.name: Physical hotplug and audible route switch
checks.observation: ADB found no Android device; macOS CoreAudio reported no devices. No physical Windows audio device was available in this environment.

remaining: Verify physical USB/Bluetooth disconnect/reconnect, actual routing and audible playback during an active voice call on Android, macOS and Windows; check the warning and fallback with VoiceOver, NVDA and TalkBack.
